resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Mount Holyoke article gives 1939 for the donation to the Commonwealth. Estuary Magazine gives 1940 for the donation, and the state park article gives June 1940 for the formal dedication. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.
Estuary says the 1938 hurricane destroyed the 1894 addition; the Mount Holyoke and state park articles say storm damage led to its demolition. All three agree the annex was lost.

The J.A. Skinner article spells the first name Joseph Allan in its body and Joseph Allen in its lead; the Mount Holyoke article says Joseph Allen. The story uses Joseph A. Skinner, matching the park's J.A. name.

sources.title: Central Watershed Outings: Summit Houses of the Pioneer Valley

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' is only partly right: the 1851 structure and 1861 addition survive as the summit house, but no source says whether the lookout room was in that part or in the 1894 annex that was demolished. The FFLA Massachusetts Facebook post on this lookout (Prospect House used as a lookout 1911-1918, now a museum) would not fetch, so it is not cited. No staffing, fire or room-access sources were found. Kind 'tower' in the brief is consistent with the register's 60-foot tower. Story names him Joseph A. Skinner because the sources spell his first name Allan and Allen. The 1821 guest cabin is now also an event in the JSON, with the fuller source quote.
